hypothesis: If Thompson's generalization holds, then across species with recorded karyotypes, most germ-cell (haploid) chromosome numbers fall between 6 and 16, with fewer species below 6 and fewer still above 16.
pass_criterion: Among all eukaryotic species (animals and plants analysed together) with a recorded haploid chromosome number n, at least 75% have 6 <= n <= 16, AND the fraction with n < 6 is under 15%, AND the fraction with n > 16 is under 15% and smaller than the fraction with n < 6. The test is repeated separately for animals and for plants, and the claim passes only if both groups meet these thresholds.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of species have 6 <= n <= 16 (in the pooled set or in either kingdom), OR the fraction with n > 16 is at least as large as the fraction with n < 6, OR either tail exceeds 25%. Results between the pass and fail thresholds are inconclusive and are reported as not confirmed.
interpretation: Thompson's 'germ-nuclei' means the reduced (gametic) chromosome number n. Where a database records only diploid 2n, n = 2n/2. 'Few' and 'fewer still' are operationalised as tail fractions below 15% (pass) or above 25% (fail), with the upper tail smaller than the lower. 'Organisms' is read in his scope of plants and animals, so fungi and protists are excluded. Modern data include many polyploid and holocentric species that were unknown in 1917. They are kept in the test because the claim is stated as a general rule. A sensitivity analysis excluding known polyploids is reported but does not decide the test. Species are counted once, using the median of their recorded values.

dataset.name: Genomes on a Tree (GoaT)
dataset.publisher: Tree of Life programme, Wellcome Sanger Institute / Earlham Institute / Darwin Tree of Life (genomehubs)
dataset.why_it_fits: GoaT aggregates curated karyotype data for animals, plants and fungi from the literature and public databases. Its web search, bulk download and REST API return per-species chromosome_number and haploid_number with taxonomic lineage, so the kingdom split and the n = 2n/2 conversion can both be done. Fields used: taxon_id, scientific_name, lineage (Metazoa vs Viridiplantae), chromosome_number, haploid_number and ploidy.
